subject: Urban Planning
title: Single-Family Zoning: America's Default
description: A 60-second lesson on Single-Family Zoning: America's Default.

hook.text: 75% of residential land in most US cities is zoned exclusively for single-family homes. No apartments allowed.

buildup.text: Single-family zoning bans duplexes, triplexes, and small apartments — even on large lots with plenty of room.

discovery.text: This creates artificial scarcity. When you can only build one home per lot, fewer homes exist and prices rise.

twist.text: Single-family zoning was used to exclude minorities. Berkeley's 1916 code was designed to keep out Chinese residents.

climax.text: Minneapolis banned single-family zoning citywide in 2018 — the first major US city to do so.

punchline.text: Most of America is illegal to build an apartment on. By design.

quiz.question: What did Minneapolis do about single-family zoning in 2018?
options: Expanded it to cover all residential neighborhoods
Banned it citywide, allowing duplexes and triplexes everywhere
Added minimum lot size requirements to existing zones
